Elena — thanks for the docs. Attached: token_modeling_sheet.xlsx (baseline + sensitivity tabs). Quick notes / next steps:

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: MAP kickoff: CareProbe evaluation & cost checks — internal analysis

Quick internal note while we wait for the traffic matrix from CareProbe. I ran the baseline numbers in token_modeling_sheet.xlsx with conservative estimates and flagged assumptions that change unit economics >15%. Summary highlights: 

- Baseline assumed per-session tokens: input 1,200 (avg prompt w/ context), output 600 => 1,800 tokens/session. If prompts average 800 tokens, cost drops ~28%.
- Caching: if 40% of requests are template-based (prefixs), prefix/KV caching reduces token consumption on average by ~30% (savings concentrated on input side). That moves hosted cost per 1M sessions down by ~25%.
- Batching: enabling 50–100ms batching window increases throughput by ~1.6–2x but adds ~25–40ms tail latency at p95; if CareProbe needs sub-200ms p95, large batching is limited. Recommend adaptive batching: aggressive during background/async flows, conservative for interactive flows.
- Model switching (fallback): serving a smaller quantized variant for high-frequency templates reduces token cost + inference cost but adds complexity in routing & evals — estimate 12–18% additional engineering effort for rollout.

Open questions we should include in MAP as gating items:
- Which user flows require interactive p95 <200ms? (limits batching)
- What % of requests are eligible for prefix caching? (affects tokens/$ heavily)
- Are there regulatory constraints on model variants (e.g., must use a verified model only)?

I'll prepare a 1-page sensitivity for the MAP showing tokens/$ across 3 scenarios (conservative, expected, optimistic). If Marcus wants, we can include a Dedicated reserved-capacity quote to compare against hosted.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Dr. Elena Soto <elena.soto@careprobe.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jason Miller <jason.miller@procurecorp.com>
Date: 2026-10-16 11:05 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: CareProbe evaluation & cost checks

Thanks — matrix attached (CareProbe_traffic_profile.csv). Quick answers: 

- Average lengths: prompt ~950 tokens, completion ~500 tokens (so ~1,450 tokens/session).
- Template %: ~35% of requests are structured templates (high chance for prefix caching).
- Peak pilot: 15 QPS sustained, burst to 40 QPS for T-minus events.
- Latency: pilot requirement p95 <= 250ms; long-term target <= 200ms.
- Decision deadline remains 10/31; procurement wants final numbers + an ops canary plan by 10/23.

We prefer hosted for pilot but are open to Dedicated if the unit-econ delta justifies it. Also attaching a quick note from procurement on contract windows.

—Elena
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Elena Soto <elena.soto@careprobe.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-19 14:02 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — due diligence: unit economics & close timeline

Elena — appreciated. Based on the matrix and our internal sensitivity (attached one-pager in the token_modeling_sheet.xlsx), here's the recommended MAP updates and the gating items we need to close by 10/23 to meet procurement's 10/31 decision: 

1) Cost sensitivity deliverable (due 10/23):
   - Final tokens/$ cases for pilot (hosted) across conservative/expected/optimistic usage.
   - Dedicated vs hosted delta for committed 6/12-month windows (take rate + reserved savings).
   - Impact of 35% template caching (you reported ~35%) and scenario w/ only 15% eligible caching.

2) Ops & canary plan (due 10/23):
   - Canary dates (pilot): Nov 8–22 window; two-week canary with traffic ramp and rollback criteria.
   - Monitoring: token-level cost breakdown, p95 latency, error/fallback rate, and cache hit ratio.

3) Technical gating questions (record in MAP):
   - Confirm interactive flows that require p95 <=200ms (limits batching).
   - Confirm whether system templates are static (eligible for persistent prefix caching) or user-generated.
   - Any requirement to avoid model switching for regulatory or audit reasons.

If CareProbe confirms the three gating items above and signs off on the canary windows, we'll produce the final MAP addendum and a pricing sensitivity pack for procurement to review. Jason — looping you for procurement timing.

Attachments: token_modeling_sheet.xlsx (sensitivity tab), MAP_addendum_outline.docx (stub)

Thanks — available for a 30m call tomorrow to walk the pack through if helpful.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
